assumptions: One reservation-instance lifetime; two already established exact keys; six grants maximum; one foreign token; old tokens remain addressable.
Fresh opaque token identities and fresh nonempty successful attempt IDs per key are represented by monotonic integers 1..3; callers supply attempt freshness, which the class does not enforce.
Two callers may share token aliases; caller identity confers no authority. Successful completion IDs are abstracted to the issuing token number; all invalid IDs form one failure outcome.
Clock is total, pure, non-reentrant and returns finite safe integers; mathematical integers model only the frozen values. Clock moves may go backward.
Ordinary native Map/WeakMap, sufficient memory, immutable token identity and no direct mutation of fields or reservation records are assumed.
Synchronous direct calls on one JavaScript agent are atomic; no method replacement, subclass overrides, hostile accessors, reentrant callbacks or concurrent shared instance.
Result objects are ordinary plain data. Failed settlement consumes its token and fences before returning failure; late, unconfirmed and invalid-ID outcomes cannot settle successfully.
Rejecting foreign/stale/duplicate token operations and invalid reserve inputs may stutter without logs; explicit fence, successful settlement and failed settlement remain separate operations.
History records successful grants and terminal token outcomes per key independently of admission slots; caller-neutral terminal events use c1 as a canonical label.
Host independently retains execution authority. cleanupConfirmed is an input label, not verified cleanup. No await occurs within a modeled operation.

Mutation is a model-only sensitivity control: none is baseline; allow-active bypasses active/fenced admission; ignore-replay bypasses replay matching. Replay matching for an unsettled predecessor accepts only the absent label, with admission normally rejecting it.
TLC finite-state exploration, its implementation, fingerprinting and the handwritten abstraction are trusted; no refinement relation or TypeScript semantics frontend is supplied.
exclusions: TypeScript proof, code-linked proof, refinement, all JavaScript numeric values, NaN, coercion, floating-point arithmetic and throwing clocks.
Key canonicalization, hashing, collision resistance, run-ID omission and proof that distinct requests have distinct keys.
OOM, native collection failures, GC/recovery or lost-token liveness, hostile object behavior and externally mutated instance state.
Actual dispatch, container/workspace deletion, grant accounting, receipts, durable claimed files, process cancellation, worker isolation and real cleanup.
Cross-process ownership, restart recovery, automatic retry, fairness, liveness, unbounded attempts or bounds beyond the frozen domains.
Symmetry reduction, state constraints, recovery, simulation and trace-depth sampling; no such exploration shortcuts are configured.
